label: rejected

evidence.V1: Rectangle with a centred doorway reads instantly from front, three-quarter and silhouette; T1 grid/tiling pass.
evidence.V2: Big wall slab, medium ashlar blocks / door frame / cap, small gold key: clear three levels.
evidence.V3: Proportions are stiff and box-like: uniform rectangular blocks, flat frame strips and a plain cap with no stylised exaggeration (no arch, no chunky voussoirs).
evidence.V4: Uniform small chamfers on every block, frame strip and cap edge catch the light in the lintel and doorway close-ups.
evidence.V5: Soft gradient smear down the inner door reveal and a dark vertical band on the end face in studio light; no z-fighting or pinches.
evidence.V6: Stone hue in 3 values plus gold accent; colourways (brick, sandstone) keep the same discipline.
evidence.V8: The gold 'keystone' is a thin flat tab stuck on the lintel and hanging below its bottom edge, not a keystone shape; the wall end face is a plain slab with no block treatment.
evidence.V9: Modular studio line correct: Anchored, Default collision for a walkable doorway, CanTouch off, Color white, grid-corner pivot, 2-stud snap.

artifacts: gradient smear on the inner door reveal
dark vertical band on the end face
top_fixes: Make the gold key a proper wedge keystone set into the lintel instead of a flat tab hanging below it
Push the shape language: arched or chunky lintel, slightly irregular block sizes
Continue the block pattern (or a cap edge) onto the end faces so tiled ends look finished
Fix normals in the door reveal so the inner faces shade flat
